chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amer, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talha ibn Zayd, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said:
An abundance of jesting takes away the dignity of one's face, an abundance of laughing erases faith, and an abundance of lying takes away one's radiance.

key_terms.الإيمان: Faith (iman) — complete religious faith and conviction
key_terms.البهاء: Radiance, splendor — the spiritual glow and majesty of a person
key_terms.المزاح: Jesting, joking — light humor that in excess undermines dignity
key_terms.ماء الوجه: Water of the face — a classical Arabic idiom for one's dignity, honor, and respectability

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about excessive joking, laughing, and lying?
ai.summary: In this Prophetic tradition transmitted through the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt Imams, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) warned against three excessive behaviors: excessive joking, excessive laughter, and excessive lying. The Arabic expression 'ma' al-wajh' (water of the face) is a classical idiom meaning one's dignity, honor, and social standing. This teaching was delivered as general moral counsel to the Muslim community, emphasizing moderation in social conduct.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (rh) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. `Amer narrated to us from his uncle `Abdillah b. `Amer from Muhammad b. Sinan from Talha b. Zayd from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
An abundance of jesting will recede the water in one’s face, and an abundance of laughing will erase one’s faith, and an abundance of lying will diminish one’s radiance.
